description: DHNx is a Python package that provides an open toolbox for building district heating and cooling network optimisation models. It belongs to the Open Energy Modelling Framework (oemof) family and is developed by the oemof developing group, whose developer guidelines it follows, with contributions welcome from anyone. The toolbox is location independent, not tied to any country: it models any district heating or cooling network whose data the user supplies, and examples in the repository show how to start. It is installed with pip from PyPI (latest upload July 2026, Python 3.10 or newer) or from the GitHub source, which had commits in August 2026, under the MIT licence at no cost. Caveats: the README describes the documentation as work in progress, the version tags remain at 0.0.x and a 0.1.0 alpha, so interfaces may still change, and the README gives no detail of the formulation, which must be read in the documentation or code. Simulation uses are optimisation and planning of heat network layouts and capacities and network flow analysis. Related records: it belongs to the same framework as model-oemof-solph and compares with model-pandapipes, which simulates heat network hydraulics.
